name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,800

entries.clue: Bit of equipment from school gym caught in zip (6)

indicatorNotes.caught in: something caught in a thing is held inside it, so C goes inside NIL

blocks.note: PE = physical education, school gym lessons
c = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A pupil pinches some kit from the school gym and gets caught with it zipped away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bit of equipment from school gym' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'school'; 'gym' starts the wordplay. 'Zip' is American slang for zero.
annotation.definitionFit: A pencil is a basic item of school equipment in every pencil case.

entries.clue: Enthusiastic when sex aid turns up right on time (9)

indicatorNotes.turns up: in a down answer, turning something up flips it to read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.on: in a down answer, one thing on another sits above it

blocks.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

annotation.surface: Someone gets very keen when a certain intimate product arrives on schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: LIEN is the hard step: a legal right to keep someone's goods until they pay you.
annotation.definitionFit: Ebullient means bubbling over with enthusiasm.

entries.clue: Bulk of cream lad mixed to make hot dip? (7)

indicatorNotes.Bulk of: the bulk of something is most of it, so CREAM loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.mixed: mixed letters are jumbled, so CREA and LAD are rearranged

annotation.surface: A kitchen instruction: blend most of the cream with a boy to produce a warm sauce for dipping.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants a food dip; the question mark warns that the 'dip' is a hollow in the ground, and a hot one because volcanoes make it.
annotation.definitionFit: A caldera is the large basin left when a volcano collapses: a dip in the land that is, or was, hot.

entries.clue: Bright student at university beginning to correct papers (5)

indicatorNotes.at: a student at university is placed beside it, so L sits next to U
indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the C of 'correct' is used

blocks.note: L = learner, as on a learner driver's plate

annotation.surface: A clever undergraduate starts marking exam scripts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Papers' looks like exam scripts in this scene, but it means identity documents, ID.
annotation.definitionFit: Lucid means clear-thinking, the sense of 'bright' for a sharp mind; both also mean shining.

entries.clue: Pig primarily investigates with nose, uprooting new problems (7)

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first of all, so only the P of 'Pig' is used
indicatorNotes.uprooting: uprooting pulls something out, so the N comes out of NUZZLES

annotation.surface: A pig roots about with its snout, digging up fresh trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uprooting' fits a pig snuffling in the soil, but it is the instruction to take out N, the usual abbreviation for new.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the plural noun sense: brain-teasers or baffling matters, things you have to work at.

entries.clue: One Piece serial ultimately broadcast for a long time (9)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of 'serial' is used
indicatorNotes.broadcast: broadcast seed is scattered, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

annotation.surface: One Piece is a Japanese anime series that has been on television for decades.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a true fact about One Piece, which has run since 1999, so 'for a long time' reads as a comment rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The Pliocene (also spelt Pleiocene) is a geological epoch, lasting about three million years.

entries.clue: Up-and-coming tech company in southeast Australia hacked computers? (7)

indicatorNotes.Up-and-coming: in a down answer, 'up' means read from the bottom, so everything is reversed
indicatorNotes.in: the company sits in the middle of the southeast-and-Australia pair

annotation.surface: A start-up tech firm in south-eastern Australia has had its computers hacked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Up-and-coming' reads as a description of a start-up, but in a down clue it is the reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A zombie is a computer taken over by a hacker and controlled remotely; the question mark flags the jargon sense.

entries.clue: Inclined to wash, disregarding cold temperature (5)

indicatorNotes.disregarding: disregarding something leaves it out, so C is dropped from CLEAN

annotation.surface: Someone is inclined to wash, but not in cold water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inclined to' reads as 'keen to', but 'Inclined' alone is the definition, the past tense of lean. C for cold is the tap marking.
annotation.definitionFit: Leant is the past tense of lean, so it means 'inclined' as in tilted.

entries.clue: Gutted sergeant prepared to be stripped of hat and uniform (6)

indicatorNotes.Gutted: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the first and last letters of 'sergeant'
indicatorNotes.to be stripped of hat: a word's hat is its top, its first letter, so READY loses R

blocks.clueFragment: prepared to be stripped of hat

annotation.surface: A disappointed sergeant expects to lose his cap and uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like military dress to go with the sergeant and the hat, but it is an adjective meaning even. 'Gutted' also means upset in British slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Steady and uniform both mean even and unvarying, as in a steady pace.

entries.clue: Headcase having row on the phone? (5)

indicatorNotes.on the phone: on the phone you only hear a word, so it is chosen by its sound

blocks.note: to scull is to row a boat

annotation.surface: A mad person rowing on the phone: a crank having an argument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Headcase' means a lunatic and 'row' an argument, but split 'Head case' and it is the bony case of the head; 'row' is rowing a boat, to scull.
annotation.definitionFit: The skull is literally the case that holds the head's brain.

entries.clue: Separation of Greek characters participating in kinky sex (6)

indicatorNotes.participating in: whatever participates in something is inside it, so CHIS goes inside SM

blocks.note: chi is a Greek letter; two or more are chis

annotation.surface: A split among Greek people who take part in unusual sex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Characters' reads as people but means letters of the alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A schism is a split, especially in a church or party.

entries.clue: Race madly to produce competition's first cracking dessert (5,4)

indicatorNotes.madly: done madly means done wildly, so the letters of RACE are jumbled
indicatorNotes.first: the first of 'competition' is its first letter, C
indicatorNotes.cracking: C cracks MAKE open and sits inside it

annotation.surface: Competitors rush to bake the winning pudding in a cooking contest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' reads as British slang for excellent, a cracking dessert, but it is the instruction to break MAKE open.
annotation.definitionFit: A cream cake is a cake filled with cream, a sweet course.

entries.clue: Difficult to hold large live weapon (7)

indicatorNotes.to hold: a word that holds others keeps them inside it

blocks.note: to be is to live, to exist

annotation.surface: A loaded, dangerous weapon is hard to grip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Live' in a weapons scene suggests live ammunition, but it is the verb, to be.
annotation.definitionFit: A halberd is a long-handled axe with a spike, carried by medieval foot soldiers.

entries.clue: Hand in dictionary that's left out (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the hand is put in the dictionary, inside OED

annotation.surface: A piece of homework handed in with a dictionary that ignores a word.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hand in' reads as one phrase meaning submit; split it and 'in' becomes the placement instruction. 'That's' just joins the definition on.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are past participles for something excluded or skipped, as a name missing from a list.

entries.clue: Bolt seat, securing last pieces of track bike build (9)

indicatorNotes.securing: the seat secures, holds, the letters inside it
indicatorNotes.last pieces of: the last pieces of three words are their last letters

blocks.note: a saddle is a bike's seat

blocks.clueFragment: last pieces of track bike build
blocks.note: last letters of trac-K, bik-E, buil-D

annotation.surface: Instructions for bolting a saddle on while finishing assembling a track bike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' reads as the verb for fastening parts in a bike workshop; here it means run off.
annotation.definitionFit: Skedaddle is informal for run away, to bolt.

entries.clue: Somebody wanted translation of Prose Edda (9)

indicatorNotes.translation of: translating turns words into new ones, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone was looking for a translation of the Prose Edda, the medieval Icelandic book of Norse myths.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Somebody wanted' reads as a person wanting a book, but 'wanted' means sought by the law, as on a Wild West poster.
annotation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, the kind of person on a wanted poster.

entries.clue: Small joke given a whirl? (4)

blocks.note: a pun is a joke on words

annotation.surface: A little joke that someone has tried out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Given a whirl' is an idiom for 'tried'; the question mark says take it literally, turned round fast.
annotation.definitionFit: Something spun has been set whirling, given a whirl in the literal sense.

entries.clue: You heard old lady picked up Finnish without opposition? (9)

indicatorNotes.heard: a word heard is chosen for its sound, so 'you' gives the letter U
indicatorNotes.picked up: in a down answer, picking something up lifts it to read bottom to top

blocks.note: Suomi is Finland's name for itself and its language

annotation.surface: Did you hear Grandma learnt Finnish without anyone objecting?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like 'learnt' in the surface, but in a down clue it lifts SUOMI to read upward.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: when everyone agrees, nobody votes against; the question mark admits it describes rather than defines.

entries.clue: Male, fending off onset of infection, comfortably piddling (6)

indicatorNotes.fending off: fending something off keeps it out, so the I is dropped from EASILY
indicatorNotes.onset of: the onset of something is its start, so only the I of 'infection' is used

blocks.clueFragment: fending off onset of infection, comfortably
blocks.note: EASILY without I, the first letter of 'infection'

annotation.surface: A man easily resisting an infection while urinating.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface steers 'piddling' towards urine and 'infection' towards illness, which also hints at the answer's measles. Piddling here means trivial.
annotation.definitionFit: Measly and piddling both mean contemptibly small.

entries.clue: State that USA incorporates after revolution (4)

indicatorNotes.incorporates: the phrase holds the answer within its letters
indicatorNotes.after revolution: a revolution turns something round, so the hidden letters read backwards

blocks.note: the letters sit across the join of 'that' and 'USA'

annotation.surface: A US state brought into the union after the American Revolution.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' points to American history, but it means turning round.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a western US state whose capital is Salt Lake City.

entries.clue: Europe supports snubbed drag act at last for Pride (7)

indicatorNotes.supports: in a down answer, a support sits underneath, so EUR goes at the bottom
indicatorNotes.snubbed: snubbed means cut short, so HAUL loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.at last: only the last letter of 'act' is used

annotation.surface: European backing for a drag show at the end of Pride month.
annotation.walkthrough: The drag act and Pride paint a Pride parade; 'drag' is the verb haul and 'Pride' is plain arrogance.
annotation.definitionFit: Hauteur is haughtiness, a proud, lofty manner.

entries.clue: Initially surveying lake, heard not a dicky bird (9)

indicatorNotes.Initially: initially means at the start, so only the S of 'surveying' is used
indicatorNotes.not: 'not a' tells you to leave the A out of the letters
indicatorNotes.dicky: dicky is British slang for faulty or unsteady, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: LAKE and HEARD, with one A removed, as fodder

annotation.surface: Watching over a lake, someone hears nothing at all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not a dicky bird' is British slang for not a word, nothing at all; split it and 'not a' removes an A, 'dicky' jumbles, and 'bird' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The sheldrake is a large duck, specifically the male shelduck.

entries.clue: Disapprove of president after empty deal is accepted (7)

indicatorNotes.after: the president comes after the rest
indicatorNotes.empty: an emptied word loses its middle, leaving D and L of 'deal'
indicatorNotes.is accepted: IS is accepted into D...L, going inside it

blocks.note: Ike, nickname of US president Dwight Eisenhower

annotation.surface: Frowning on a president once a hollow agreement has been signed off.
annotation.walkthrough: The IS inside D...L is the clue's own word 'is', not the verb it pretends to be.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: both verbs express a negative view of something, dislike leaning to taste and disapprove to judgement.

entries.clue: Policeman arrests vile criminal in hip area (6)

indicatorNotes.arrests: the policeman arrests, holds, the letters inside PC
indicatorNotes.criminal: criminal letters are bent out of shape, so VILE is rearranged

annotation.surface: A cop arrests a nasty villain in a trendy part of town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hip area' reads as a fashionable neighbourhood; it is the body's hip region.
annotation.definitionFit: Pelvic means of the pelvis, the bony hip area.

entries.clue: English artist certain for cancellation (7)

blocks.note: RA = Royal Academician, a British artist

annotation.surface: An English artist is sure to be cancelled.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface hints at cancel culture; Erasure is also an English pop duo, a red herring for 'English artist'.
annotation.definitionFit: An erasure is a deletion, a cancellation of what was written.

entries.clue: Something cheeky Independent welcomed in surface (5)

indicatorNotes.welcomed in: a guest welcomed in goes inside, so I goes inside ARSE

blocks.note: British slang for bottom, whose cheeks make it 'cheeky'
I = Independent, as in election results

annotation.surface: A rude item finds its way into the newspaper, the Independent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Surface' is the verb: to come up, arise. 'Something cheeky' is a playful way of pointing at buttocks.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: problems or a diver come up into view, emerge.

entries.clue: After money's spent in hobby, succeeded making baked goods (7)

indicatorNotes.After: the S comes after the rest
indicatorNotes.spent: money spent is gone, so M leaves PASTIME

annotation.surface: Someone who spends money on a hobby finally succeeds at baking.
annotation.walkthrough: A pasty is a British pastry case folded around a savoury filling.
annotation.definitionFit: Pasties are folded pastries filled and baked.

entries.clue: Trial drug, snorting one line (5)

indicatorNotes.snorting: whatever is snorted goes inside, so I and L go inside POT

annotation.surface: A drug trial where a participant snorts a line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Line' in a drug scene suggests cocaine, but it is the plain abbreviation L.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used as a noun or modifier: a pilot scheme or TV pilot tests something before the full launch.

entries.clue: Message imparted by animated movie about cocaine trouble (9)

indicatorNotes.animated: animated means brought to lively motion, so MOVIE's letters are moved
indicatorNotes.about: the rearranged MOVIE goes about, around, C

annotation.surface: A cartoon film carries a warning about the harm cocaine does.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Animated movie' reads as a cartoon, but 'animated' is the instruction to rearrange MOVIE.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a spoken recording left on a phone is one kind of message.

entries.clue: One working to stop tracks like heavy metal? (5)

indicatorNotes.to stop: ON stops, plugs, the gap in RY by going inside it

annotation.surface: A musician who blocks out heavy-metal tracks.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about music, but IRONY here is not sarcasm: it is the adjective 'of iron', and iron is a heavy metal.
annotation.definitionFit: Irony (pronounced like iron-y) means containing or resembling iron; the question mark flags this rare sense.

entries.clue: See you in port on Red Sea, nude (7)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across answer, a word on another comes after it
indicatorNotes.nude: a nude word is stripped of its outer letters, leaving the E of 'Sea'

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the famous revolutionary, a Red
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port

annotation.surface: Goodbye, see you at a Red Sea port, where people go naked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Red Sea' is a single place in the surface; split it into 'Red' for CHE and 'Sea' for its middle letter. Cheerio is a British goodbye.
annotation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British farewell, just like 'see you'.

entries.clue: Very small letter and flower personal assistant dismissed (6)

indicatorNotes.dismissed: the dismissed PA is sent away from PANSY

blocks.note: tee = the letter T spelt out

annotation.surface: A tiny note and a bunch of flowers for a PA who has been sacked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flower' here really is a flower, the pansy; the trick is that the PA comes out of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, informal and childlike, as in 'a teensy bit'.
